name: Gorilla / ToolBench (original)
decomposition_method: Gorilla: essentially no decomposition — single-intent API selection; a prompt maps to one correct API call, optionally grounded by retrieved API documentation (Retriever-Aware Training, RAT). ToolBench/ToolLLM: LLM-prompted multi-step decomposition via DFSDT (depth-first search-based decision tree) — ChatGPT/ToolLLaMA expands and backtracks over a tree of reasoning/action steps to find a valid solution path; instruction-tuning data also covers single-tool and multi-tool scenarios.
decomposition_granularity: tool call (API call). Gorilla = one API call per instruction. ToolBench = a chain/sequence of API calls (a solution path of tool calls) per instruction.
ordering_strategy: Gorilla: single call, no ordering. ToolBench: dynamic tree search (DFSDT) — depth-first with backtracking; the model can retract a step and try another branch, effectively re-planning the sequence mid-search rather than committing to a fixed order.
decomposition_validation: Gorilla: validation is by AST sub-tree match against ground truth plus an AST-based hallucination check (did it invoke a real, in-domain API). ToolBench: validation of a solution path is by ToolEval — Pass Rate (did the trajectory complete the instruction within an API-call budget) and Preference/Win Rate (LLM judge prefers one trajectory over another). DFSDT itself provides search-time pruning (abandon dead branches) but there is no separate completeness/non-redundancy detector + reward model.
hierarchy_depth: Gorilla: flat (single call). ToolBench: multi-level tree — DFSDT explores a decision tree of multi-step tool trajectories; multi-tool instructions are organized intra-category and intra-collection, giving a hierarchical tool/category structure.
router_type: Gorilla: retrieve-then-(generate) — a document retriever (BM25 / GPT-Index) selects candidate API docs, then the model emits the call; functionally a retrieve-then-select single-label picker. ToolBench: graph/tree planner — DFSDT plans a multi-step trajectory, with a neural API retriever recommending APIs per instruction. [uncertain]
routing_model: Gorilla: fine-tuned LLaMA (7B) with retriever-aware fine-tuning + external embedding/BM25 retriever. ToolBench: ToolLLaMA (fine-tuned LLaMA) plus a trained neural API retriever; data generated/annotated by ChatGPT. Both combine a fine-tuned LLM with embedding-similarity retrieval.
handles_ambiguity: Gorilla: best-effort pick — RAT trains the model to reason over (possibly wrong) retrieved docs and pick the most suitable API, but no explicit abstain/clarify mechanism. ToolBench: best-effort via DFSDT backtracking (try alternate branch if a path fails); no clarification-request or abstention modeling. Neither benchmark scores when-to-ask. [uncertain]
fallback_behavior: Gorilla: no explicit fallback — produces its best API call (errors surface as AST mismatch/hallucination). ToolBench: implicit retry via DFSDT backtracking to another branch; if no path completes within the call budget the instruction is scored as failed (Pass Rate 0). No human-escalation path. [uncertain]
skill_pool_scale_and_retrieval: Gorilla: ~1,600-1,700+ ML APIs (TorchHub, TensorHub, HuggingFace) in APIBench; embedding/BM25 retrieval (top-k API docs) injected into the prompt — explicitly studies zero-shot (no docs) vs. retrieval-aware settings. ToolBench: very large pool — 16,464 real-world RESTful APIs / 3,451 tools across 49 categories from RapidAPI; a trained neural API retriever (plus oracle retriever) selects relevant APIs before reasoning. Both are designed to scale routing to hundreds-to-thousands of tools via retrieval.
router_agent_asymmetry: Not explicitly modeled; the same fine-tuned model both consumes retrieved docs and emits calls. Gorilla's RAT does expose the model to retrieved (sometimes wrong) documentation, but there is no formal router-vs-agent information split. [uncertain]
execution_pattern: Gorilla: single API call (one-shot), evaluated structurally (no live execution required for AST metric). ToolBench: sequential multi-step chain executed against live RapidAPI endpoints, driven by DFSDT tree search (with backtracking) — closest to a ReAct/tree-search loop, one tool at a time.
parallel_vs_concurrent: Neither targets parallel/concurrent tool calls. Gorilla = single call. ToolBench = strictly sequential multi-step (DFSDT explores one path at a time). No parallel-in-one-turn or concurrent execution concept.
dependency_detection: No explicit dependency detection. Gorilla = single call (N/A). ToolBench = assumed-sequential; DFSDT discovers an ordering empirically through search rather than computing a dependency DAG up front. [uncertain]
result_aggregation: Gorilla: N/A (single call). ToolBench: iterative — each tool's returned result feeds the next reasoning/action step in the DFSDT trajectory; the final answer is produced by the model after the solution path, judged holistically by ToolEval rather than via a typed structured merge.
mid_chain_feedback: Gorilla: none (single shot). ToolBench: hard mid-chain feedback — DFSDT explicitly uses observed tool outputs to decide whether to proceed, retract a step, or branch to a different action, i.e. real-time re-planning during the search.
benchmark_name: Gorilla -> APIBench (TorchHub / TensorHub / HuggingFace ML APIs) evaluated with AST accuracy + hallucination rate. ToolLLM -> ToolBench dataset evaluated with ToolEval (Pass Rate + Win Rate). These ARE the benchmarks (predecessors to BFCL v3).
multi_intent_coverage: Gorilla/APIBench: single-intent only (one API per instruction) — establishes the single-intent baseline. ToolBench: yes — includes single-tool and multi-tool instructions (intra-category and intra-collection multi-tool), i.e. compound/sequential multi-intent tasks, but not labeled parallel vs. sequential the way BFCL is.
accuracy_metric: Gorilla/APIBench: AST sub-tree matching (structural function-call correctness) + AST-based hallucination metric (penalizes invented/out-of-domain APIs). ToolBench/ToolEval: outcome-style automated metrics — Pass Rate (task completed within an API-call budget) and Win Rate / Preference (ChatGPT judge picks the better trajectory; validated at ~87% pass-rate and ~80% win-rate agreement with humans).
clarification_capability: Not measured by either benchmark. No when-to-ask vs. when-to-answer scoring, no clarification-efficiency metric. (Predates the ClarifyBench/InteractComp line of work.)
process_vs_outcome_eval: Gorilla: structural/process-leaning (scores the produced call structure via AST, not a downstream outcome). ToolBench/ToolEval: outcome-oriented — Pass Rate (did it complete) and Win Rate (overall trajectory preference) judge the end result/whole trajectory rather than supervising each intermediate step with a process reward.
eval_stability: Gorilla/APIBench AST evaluation is offline and reproducible. ToolBench is a known stability problem: it calls live RapidAPI endpoints, so API drift/downtime causes non-reproducible Pass/Win rates — this instability is exactly what later work (StableToolBench, with a virtual/cached API server) was built to fix.
integration_pattern: Gorilla: in-context / prompted model + external retriever, distributed as an open-source model and APIBench eval. ToolBench/ToolLLM: standalone open platform for training, serving, and evaluating tool-use LLMs (data pipeline + ToolLLaMA + API retriever + ToolEval). Both are research artifacts, integrated as model+eval suites rather than production routing middleware.
routing_layer: Application/model layer — both operate at the LLM+retriever level (prompt-time API selection); no inference-engine-layer routing.
latency_overhead: Gorilla: low — one retrieval + one generation per instruction. ToolBench: high — DFSDT explores many branches with live API round-trips per step, so the solution-path search incurs substantial latency and API-call cost (Pass Rate is even defined relative to a call budget). [uncertain]
online_adaptation: Static. Gorilla adapts to new/updated APIs at test time via Retriever-Aware Training (retriever supplies current docs) but does not learn from production feedback. ToolBench is a fixed dataset/benchmark with no online adaptation; ToolLLaMA is trained once via supervised fine-tuning on the generated data.
adoption: Open-source and highly influential. Gorilla (UC Berkeley, NeurIPS 2024; arXiv 2305.15334) — open model + APIBench; spawned the Gorilla project and BFCL. ToolLLM/ToolBench (OpenBMB, ICLR 2024 spotlight; arXiv 2307.16789) — open platform, 16k+ APIs, canonical early tool-use benchmark. Both are widely cited baselines now largely superseded by BFCL v3 (and StableToolBench for stability).
